rated_messages.input_message: When you begin to crave a cig, concentrate on your reasons for not smoking. Keep a list on your phone and look at it when you feel yourself beginning to falter.
When a craving hits, keep your hands busy by doing the dishes or taking out the trash. Small chores will help pass the time during a craving.
Sometimes an urge comes on like a wave. Imagine what it is like to ride the wave as it ebbs and flows. Instead of trying to swim against it, try riding it out until it disappears into the sea.
If you find sounds soothing, tune in to the soundtrack of nature, like crashing waves, the wind rustling through trees, or birds singing.
Instead of lighting up a cigarette, light a scented candle or burn some incense.
Practice staying in this location without smoking. Just notice your urge. Practicing this will weaken this trigger with time. Just think of it as practice.
Some places trigger powerful cravings, that is to be expected. Stop and notice where in your body you feel those cravings and remind yourself that cravings typically pass in 1 to 3 minutes
Crumple a piece of paper into a ball and imagine it is your urge. Toss the "urge" into the garbage or against the wall. By doing this, you are letting go of your urges.

If you find yourself thinking: "I can't do this", "I need a cig", or "I'll just have one", make sure you tell yourself "I absolutely CAN do this", "I'm in control". Take control of your negative thoughts!
Imagine your 'you' from next year has come to visit, and guess what? You quit! How good is that?
